articles.title: Cinnabar’s five touchdown drives overwhelm Mt. Silver
articles.dek: Gholdengo completed thirty-three passes as the Blaze won 38–24. Arcanine scored twice before a three-week injury report complicated the next assignment.
articles.author: dorian-pike

body.text: Cinnabar scored touchdowns on its first five full offensive possessions against Mt. Silver. The Blaze went seventy-three yards, eighty-one, seventy-eight, seventy-two and eighty, with a halftime kneel separating the third march from the fourth. Gholdengo kept completing passes, the backs kept finishing, and an opponent that arrived 13–1 eventually ran out of immediate answers. Cinnabar won 38–24 and reached ten wins with a second consecutive victory over a division leader.

I have spent enough time asking Blaine’s team to begin its good work before the score becomes desperate. This afternoon supplies the requested correction. Cinnabar led 21–14 at halftime, scored fourteen unanswered points in the third quarter and made the Reds chase a twenty-one-point deficit. The Blaze beat Blackthorn 31–19 a week ago. Their current argument includes two substantial opponents and sixty-nine points scored against them.

Gholdengo completed thirty-three of forty-one passes for 357 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Arcanine ran for fifty yards and two scores, adding fifty receiving yards. Buizel scored on the ground and through the air. The offense gained 424 yards, converted five of eight third downs and punted once. Those are the measures of how often Cinnabar made the next possession useful.

“We expected to move the ball,” Gholdengo said. “When they answered, we went back to work. I wanted the next throw.” The quarterback’s confidence had plenty of support. Nine different teammates caught a pass, and the offense recovered from the few situations in which the Reds seemed close to ending a drive.
Cinnabar answered two Lynch touchdowns

The Blaze’s first possession began with two short-left completions to Thievul and included nineteen yards through the air to Arcanine. Exploud’s fifteen-yard catch brought the offense close enough for Buizel to finish. He ran right for seven yards with 3:20 left in the first quarter, and Charjabug’s extra point supplied a 7–0 lead.

Garshawn Lynch answered emphatically. His thirty-yard run began the next Mt. Silver drive, and his twelve-yard touchdown up the middle finished it. The Reds had moved sixty-six yards to tie the game. Lynch would finish with 113 rushing yards on eight carries, a striking amount of production from a limited number of attempts. He gave Connor McLarren a way to match Cinnabar early even as the passing game struggled to find regular completions.

The next Blaze possession immediately encountered trouble. Blayz Matthews sacked Gholdengo for six yards, and Mach Singltery broke up the following pass. On third-and-sixteen, Gholdengo found Archaludon deep right for twenty-five. Cinnabar later converted third-and-four with a twenty-four-yard completion to Exploud. Two chances to end the drive became large gains instead.

Thievul caught the one-yard touchdown with 4:37 left in the second quarter, completing an eighty-one-yard march. Lynch answered again, this time breaking a forty-five-yard touchdown run through the middle. Mt. Silver had tied it at fourteen. The Reds were still keeping pace, but Cinnabar had already demonstrated that forcing a long third down would not automatically send its offense away.

body.alt: Garchomp #22. Garshawn Lynch’s forty-five-yard touchdown run brought Mt. Silver level at 14–14 after the extra point.
body.caption: Garshawn Lynch’s forty-five-yard touchdown run brought Mt. Silver level at 14–14 after the extra point.

body.text: Buizel finished the difficult possession

Gholdengo opened the ensuing drive with two incompletions intended for Arcanine. He returned to the same receiver on third-and-ten and gained twenty-three yards. That decision kept a seventy-eight-yard touchdown possession alive and began another sequence in which the Blaze distributed the work. Thievul, Wigglytuff and Skiploom supplied catches; Gholdengo himself converted a third-and-one with a two-yard run.

Near the end of the half, Cinnabar faced third-and-eleven. A pass to Buizel had been broken up, and a short throw to Arcanine lost a yard. Gholdengo then found Buizel deep left for a fourteen-yard touchdown with forty-five seconds remaining. The Blaze had moved ahead 21–14 by recovering from two distinct long-yardage situations on the same drive.

“I wanted the next chance as soon as the first one was gone,” Buizel said. “There was another play to run.” His eagerness was rewarded. He had finished the opening drive on the ground and now finished the last meaningful Cinnabar drive of the half through the air. Two different assignments had produced touchdowns from the same back.

body.alt: Buizel #16. Buizel caught a fourteen-yard touchdown pass late in the first half.
body.caption: Buizel caught a fourteen-yard touchdown pass late in the first half.

body.text: Mt. Silver gained nine yards on its next first down, then encountered number 48 Thievul twice. He broke up consecutive throws to Gregar Jenings on second-and-one and third-and-one. The Reds punted, and Cinnabar knelt to end the half. The receiver wearing 45 had scored earlier; the defender wearing 48 had helped protect the lead. Keeping the two Thievul contributions separate improves the account considerably.
Arcanine turned seven points into twenty-one

Cinnabar opened the third quarter with three consecutive completions: eleven yards to Exploud, twenty-seven to number 45 Thievul and seventeen to Beautifly. Arcanine then ran three times, finishing the drive with a five-yard touchdown to the right. The offense had gone seventy-two yards without facing a third down and moved ahead 28–14.

The Reds found a first down on their answer but stalled when Mawile sacked Jacoby Brizzet on third-and-two. After the punt, Cinnabar drove eighty yards in six plays. Thievul caught fourteen and nineteen yards around Archaludon’s twenty-seven-yard reception. Arcanine finished with a seventeen-yard run to the left, and Charjabug made it 35–14 with 1:04 remaining in the quarter.

Arcanine’s current injury report lists three weeks, a substantial cost attached to a productive afternoon. The recorded game does not timestamp the injury. His fifty rushing yards, fifty receiving yards and two touchdowns describe what Cinnabar received here; they also explain why Blaine’s preparation for Celadon now includes replacing more than a single kind of offensive work.

“The other guys did a lot to get us there,” Arcanine said. “I’m happy the runs helped.” The reserved answer leaves room to recognize those contributors. Thievul caught ten of eleven targets for ninety-six yards and a touchdown. Archaludon caught all three of his targets for fifty-nine. Gholdengo repeatedly found useful gains before asking the backfield to finish.
Mt. Silver recovered ten points, then ran out of time

The strangest turnover sequence arrived late in the third quarter. Number 48 Thievul intercepted a deep-right pass, then fumbled, and Gregar Jenings recovered for Mt. Silver. The Reds retained an opportunity, but Primeape sacked Brizzet for seven yards on the next snap. Crem Ftzpatrik completed a four-yard pass and then threw incomplete. Mt. Silver punted again.

Brizzet returned to the passing record in the fourth quarter and led a seventy-five-yard touchdown drive. A thirty-one-yard completion to Ariados converted third-and-ten, and a four-yard pass to Lynch finished the march. Lynch had supplied both early rushing touchdowns and now the receiving score. The extra point reduced the margin to 35–21.

Cinnabar then supplied an avoidable opening. Arcanine fumbled the ensuing kickoff return, and Weepinbell recovered for Mt. Silver. The Reds moved the ball far enough for his twenty-three-yard field goal, cutting the deficit to eleven. Glalie recovered the subsequent onside kick for Cinnabar, and the Blaze used their next possession to reach a forty-three-yard Charjabug field goal with 1:59 left. The margin was fourteen again.

“They were considerate enough to let us back near it,” McLarren said. “Unfortunately, they had already spent three quarters completing passes. We should try being less hospitable when somebody needs sixteen yards.” His defense allowed twenty first downs. Brizzet finished sixteen of thirty-five for 172 yards, one touchdown and one interception; the Reds’ passing game could not sustain the pace their early rushing explosions had established.

Mt. Silver also received a twelve-week injury report for Ariados after his five catches for fifty-six yards. Tic Thorpe and Josh Alakazam remain unavailable with five and six reported weeks respectively. The Reds travel to Azalea at 13–2 with both offensive availability and defensive third-down execution demanding attention. Cinnabar visits Celadon at 10–5, carrying two consecutive wins and a newly difficult backfield adjustment. Blaine has strong evidence to build on: five sustained touchdown drives against a thirteen-win opponent, with thirty-three completed passes doing much of the work.
